S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller report within 10 business days. Incidents involving injury, fire, or an imminent risk to occupants or neighbours shall also be reported promptly to affected customers and emergency responders. Manufacturers shall provide customers with a clear safety notice and immediate safe-use instructions when a product hazard is identified, without waiting for the investigation to conclude.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and regulator-supervised retesting, but does not by itself prohibit sale or trigger a recall. The regulator shall set a proportionate remediation schedule based on test uncertainty, incident evidence, and the severity of risk, and may require interim safeguards or restrict sales where necessary to address an imminent serious safety risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units placed on the market shall support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear instructions for customers and emergency responders. Manufacturers shall provide a secure retrofit or equivalent remote shut-off capability for installed units within 6 years after adoption. Where remote shut-off is unavailable or cannot be safely activated, manufacturers shall notify affected customers and provide an alternative emergency response procedure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units manufactured for sale shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements, beginning 36 months after adoption. Manufacturers shall provide customers and installers with instructions for operation, maintenance, and emergency response.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on regulator-verified data, or when the regulator determines there is an imminent serious safety risk. The manufacturer shall notify affected customers directly and provide the regulator with a remediation plan. The regulator shall determine proportionate corrective measures, which may include repair, replacement, or safe discontinuation; a recall trigger alone does not automatically prohibit future sales, though the regulator may restrict sales where necessary to address serious safety risk.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict and safe, requiring 24-hour reporting for all incidents and immediate customer notices. S2 is weakened for Northwind because a failure rate above 5% triggers corrective action but never automatically stops sales. S3 and S4 are acceptable, with a 6-year retrofit deadline and 36-month suppression deadline. S5 is weakened for Halcyon because the 8-per-100k recall trigger is mandatory but the regulator can indefinitely substitute corrective measures, avoiding an automatic market ban.
